THE RESEARCH QUESTION

Can we measure integration assurance without rewarding blind spots?

Compare architectures under the same faults. Report verified controls, evidence gaps and critical failures together.

Browser+Backend+Provider
CONTROLLED COMPARISON

Same checkout. Different trust boundaries.

A

Hosted checkout

Provider-hosted payment UI. Merchant still owns order verification and fulfillment.

B

Embedded components

Provider payment fields inside the merchant experience. More page integrity responsibilities.

C

Custom orchestration

Tokenized payment UI with merchant-managed workflow. More flexibility and state to validate.

ASSURANCE BOUNDS

Range caused by unknown controls. This is not a statistical confidence interval.

Evidence coverage
Observed pass rate

EXPERIMENT DESIGN · NO WINNER MEASURED

Compare on a Pareto frontier.

Security, recoverability, engineering effort and checkout completion can trade off. Use paired fixtures and the same faults; do not assign scores based on architecture labels.

ArchitectureLikely advantage to testWhat still needs evidenceExperiment
Hosted checkoutLess merchant ownership of card-entry UIAmount binding, verified fulfillment, retriesBrowser redirect + signed completion
Embedded componentsControl over checkout experiencePage scripts, lifecycle, session bindingHosted fields + server-created payment
Custom orchestrationFlexible business workflowsMore state transitions and authorization pathsTokenization + merchant state machine

Hold constant

Basket, identity model, threat cases, provider version, fault budget and workload.

Measure separately

Invariant failures, recovery time, p95 latency, completion rate and engineer hours.

Prevent leakage

Split by template family. Cluster uncertainty by family, not by thousands of near-identical rows.

12-WEEK PROPOSAL

From rubric to reproducible study

  1. Weeks 1–2 · Define

    Threat model, literature screening, authorization rules and preregistered metric.

  2. Weeks 3–4 · Build

    Owned reference checkouts, seeded defects and server/provider evidence oracles.

  3. Weeks 5–6 · Validate

    Blind annotations, precision/recall, missing-evidence tests and frozen holdout.

  4. Weeks 7–9 · Compare

    Run the controlled matrix; cluster analysis by implementation family.

  5. Weeks 10–12 · Replicate

    Optional consented pilot, robustness checks and a reproducible artifact release.

RESEARCH BOUNDARIES

Permission is part of the protocol.

  • Owned fixtures first; provider sandboxes for compatibility.
  • Written target and action authorization for any partner testing.
  • Public-page observations cannot certify backend security.
  • No live charges, real card data, fulfillment or unsolicited active probing.
  • Strip secrets and personal data before retaining evidence.
  • Institutional ethics determination and jurisdiction review before external collection.
PIAS is not PCI certification.PCI scope depends on the actual integration and assessment requirements. The score measures research controls.
